base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

revision.description: The diff `new_revision` the client reviewed. A changed revision refuses with `stale_revision`.

base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

body.description: The new draft. Blank text removes the draft, and a new blank thread is not created.

base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

revision.description: The diff `new_revision` the client reviewed. A changed revision refuses with `stale_revision`.

input_view.description: Public input View projection. Routing, validation rules and secret-storage flags stay at the host; created_at and origin are engine stamps.

input_origin.description: The session that asks. A form from a child session also names its parent, because it reaches every ancestor session.

lane.description: One bar of a timeline. Times are epoch milliseconds. A lane without end still runs, and end is never before start.

anchor.description: A diff line that a thread belongs to: the file path, the old or new side and the 1-based line on that side.

author.description: Who wrote a message. The host sets it from the authenticated caller; a client never sends it.

message.description: One posted message of a thread.

thread.description: A discussion with stable message ids. `draft` is the saved, unsent text of the human.

submission_status.description: The delivery stage of one Send: stored, handed to the owner, in work, answered or failed.

submission.description: The host receipt of one Send. The id stays the same for every retry with the same idempotency key.

values.description: The non-secret values of the inputs that the Send collected.

idempotency_key.description: A client key that makes a retried Send return the first submission.

app_attachment.description: The attachment row of an app. Its bytes hold the opening picture; the live view holds the current state.

shortcut_key.description: One key that an app shortcut binds: one printable ASCII character from `!` to `~` (case-sensitive, so `A` is Shift+a) or one named key. Modifiers are never bindable. `Escape` and `Tab` stay with the surface.

shortcut.description: One app shortcut. It sends the `action` id to the owner code, or presses the button or selectable card `node_id` like a click.

label.description: The short text that a surface shows in its shortcut legend.

action.description: The id that the owner code receives in a `shortcut` event.

node_id.description: A button or a selectable card of the app. A surface presses it as a click.

command_icon.description: A picture that a surface can show instead of the label of a diff toolbar command. The label stays the accessible name.

reveals.description: The key of another app of the same owner and session. When a person activates the node, the surface shows that app. It waits for the app to open.

line_tones.description: Optional tones aligned with lines; null means plain text.

is_selected.description: The choice that holds now. A menu of a diff toolbar marks it, and a press chooses it again.

children.description: The toolbar of the diff. A button is one action. A group of buttons is one menu, and its label names the current choice.

oneOf.description: A picture. With `before`, the surface compares the old picture with the new one.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a person who cannot see it.

before.description: The old picture. Absent means a single picture.

oneOf.description: A 3D picture that the owner describes and every surface draws. x points right, y up and z to the viewer; the camera fits the rectangle from (0, 0) to (width, height) at z = 0.

fov.description: The vertical field of view in degrees. 0 is an orthographic camera.

is_wrapping.description: True when an object that leaves one edge comes back at the other. A surface then eases it the short way.

tick_ms.description: How long a surface eases an object to its new place. 0 jumps.

public_component.description: A component as the input View projection shows it. Validation rules and secret-storage flags stay at the host.

live_owner.description: Host-stamped Activity invocation and optional persistent history that own a live view.

placement.description: Where a live view shows. `attachment` makes a durable app attachment: it outlives the call that opened it and keeps its state after a restart.

inline.description: Show the app in the chat turn that opened it.

session.description: Where the session apps button opens the app: beside the chat, in the chat area, or not at all.

picture.description: One picture as base64 data. The data holds at most 2 MiB of picture bytes; JSON makes it 4/3 larger. An app always sends `data`; only the picture that the model reads has `bytes` in its place. `x-vis-magic` lists the first bytes of each media type: a picture matches one list, and each entry of that list is hex bytes at an offset. The header may hold at most `x-vis-max-pixels` pixels.

bytes.description: Set by the host in the picture that the model reads: the size of the picture in bytes. The model never reads `data`.

width.description: The picture width in pixels. The host reads it from the picture header; a value from the owner must match.

height.description: The picture height in pixels. The host reads it from the picture header; a value from the owner must match.

log_level.description: How serious one app log entry is.

log_entry.description: One entry of the debug log of an app. The host numbers the entries and stamps the time. A writer may send longer text: the host cuts it by code points. A long `message` keeps its start and ends with `…`. A long `detail` keeps its start and its end, joined by a line with `…`. A blank `detail` is dropped.

at.description: Milliseconds since the epoch when the host took the entry.

source.description: `app` for an entry that the owner wrote; `host` for an entry that Vis wrote, for example a failed callback.

detail.description: More text, for example a stack trace.

app_scope.description: Who an app belongs to. A `session` app belongs to the session that opened it. A `global` app belongs to no session: only an SDK program opens it, through `POST /v1/apps`.

extension.description: The extension that owns this panel view.

surfaces.description: Where an app shows. The opener declares the defaults. A reader gets the values after the person's settings. Only an app takes surfaces.

settings_key.description: The id prefix of the settings of this app: `<settings_key>_inline` and `<settings_key>_session`. Only an app with a key has them.

scope.description: Who this app belongs to. Absent means `session`. Only an app takes a scope, and a `global` app needs a key.

is_persistent.description: Whether a global app comes back after a gateway restart, as a stale picture until its owner adopts it by key. Absent means true. Only a global app takes it.

is_stale.description: True for the saved picture of an owned view after a gateway restart, until its extension loads again.

is_archived.description: True when the owner archived this app. It keeps its state and leaves the default lists.

is_closed.description: True when the owner closed this app. It keeps its last state and takes no more actions.

shortcuts.description: The keyboard shortcuts of an app, with unique keys. Only an app takes shortcuts.

agent_note.description: The app state that the model reads with the next user message. Only an app takes a note.

submissions.description: The newest Send receipts of an app, oldest first.

log.description: The newest debug log entries of an app, oldest first. Only an app takes a log.

detail.description: Blank text clears the status' detail; a declaration omits it instead.

tone.description: Semantic styling for every line in this append; log nodes only.

oneOf.description: Replace every row of a table at once. Selected ids whose rows are gone are dropped.

shortcuts.description: The new shortcut list. It replaces the old list, and an empty list removes every shortcut.

text.description: The new note for the model. It replaces the old note, and a blank text removes the note.

message.description: The message, up to 4 times the entry bound. The host first redacts secrets and then cuts the text to the entry bound, so a cut never splits a labelled secret.

detail.description: More text, for example a stack trace, up to 4 times the entry bound. The host first redacts secrets and then cuts the text to the entry bound.

at.description: Set by the host: the time of the entry.

source.description: Set by the host: `app` for an owner patch, `host` for an entry of Vis.

input_result.description: Public input close receipt. Submitted values and secret handles are returned only to the waiting extension, never to the event stream.

live_close.description: Public live close receipt. SSE may omit the already-streamed view; consumers retain the picture assembled from open and patch events. Journal polling may include the settled view.

scene_builtin_mesh.description: A mesh that every scene knows without a declaration. Each vertex lies inside the unit cube; each face is a triangle in counter-clockwise order seen from outside. Both surfaces read these arrays, so a shape looks the same on every screen.

scene_mesh.description: A mesh that one scene declares: triangles in counter-clockwise order seen from outside, so a surface can drop the back faces.

scene_object.description: One object of a scene: a mesh with a place, a turn, a size and a colour.

mesh.description: A built-in mesh name or the id of a mesh that the scene declares.

rx.description: Rotation about the x axis in degrees. A surface turns about x, then y, then z.

is_emissive.description: True paints the full colour without light, as a glow.

scene_object_change.description: A change of one scene object. Keys that it leaves out keep their value. A new id needs a `mesh`.

mesh.description: A built-in mesh name or the id of a mesh that the scene declares.

rx.description: Rotation about the x axis in degrees. A surface turns about x, then y, then z.

is_emissive.description: True paints the full colour without light, as a glow.
